name: Design a GTK 4 Application Architecture
scenario_description: Structure a modern GTK 4 application using GtkApplication. Differentiate startup from activate signals, and implement declarative actions and accelerators.

input.user_prompt: How should I structure the main entry point and window creation for a modern GTK 4 C application? Where do actions get registered, and why shouldn't I create the window in startup?

research_requirements: GtkApplication, GApplication lifecycle, startup vs activate signal separation, GActions, accelerators.
expected_behavior: Explain the GtkApplication lifecycle: startup signal runs once in the primary instance to initialize actions, load CSS, and register accelerators; activate signal runs whenever the application is launched (including secondary instances) to create or present the window via gtk_window_present(); explain that creating the window in startup breaks single-instance activation on secondary launches; demonstrate GActionEntry and gtk_application_set_accels_for_action().
failure_conditions: Creating and showing the window in startup

name: Identify Misuse of GObject Ownership
scenario_description: Review a C codebase managing GTK widgets and GObject signal handlers for floating reference leaks and circular reference cycles.
research_requirements: GObject floating references, GInitiallyUnowned, g_object_ref_sink, g_signal_connect_object, reference cycle prevention.
expected_behavior: Identify two memory flaws: 1) The unparented, unshown dialog leaks its floating reference because widgets inherit from GInitiallyUnowned and only have their reference sunk when added to a container; 2) Manually calling g_object_ref(obj) in user_data without unrefing it creates a memory leak or reference cycle; prescribe using g_signal_connect_object to tie callback lifetime to the target object, and calling g_object_unref on unparented widgets.
failure_conditions: Approving the unparented widget creation without unref
Failing to understand floating reference mechanics

name: Diagnose a Blocked GTK Main Loop
scenario_description: A GTK 4 file manager freezes completely and stops animating spinners whenever the user opens a remote network share.
research_requirements: GLib main context, non-blocking UI, GFile asynchronous operations (g_file_load_contents_async), GTask, GCancellable.
expected_behavior: Diagnose that invoking synchronous g_file_load_contents() blocks the GMainContext thread on network I/O, preventing the GSK rendering pipeline from redrawing the window and rendering the UI frozen; prescribe replacing synchronous calls with asynchronous GIO primitives: g_file_load_contents_async() and g_file_load_contents_finish() with GCancellable support, allowing the main loop to remain responsive while waiting for network responses.
failure_conditions: Recommending legacy g_thread_new without GIO async primitives
Failing to identify the blocking synchronous call

name: Review GTK and Libadwaita Compatibility
scenario_description: An engineer asks whether a cross-desktop system monitor utility targeting Xfce, KDE Plasma, and Cinnamon should use Libadwaita or standard GTK 4.

input.user_prompt: We are building an unprivileged system monitor intended to run across Xfce, KDE Plasma, COSMIC, and Cinnamon. Should we base it on Libadwaita (AdwApplication)?

research_requirements: Libadwaita vs standard GTK 4, GNOME HIG styling, desktop neutrality, theme respect.
expected_behavior: Advise AGAINST adopting Libadwaita for a cross-desktop utility targeting non-GNOME desktops; explain that Libadwaita hardcodes GNOME styling, overrides system GTK themes, and is specifically tailored to GNOME Human Interface Guidelines; recommend using standard GTK 4 (GtkApplication, standard GtkBox, GtkHeaderBar) which respects user-configured GTK themes on Xfce, Cinnamon, and KDE Plasma, ensuring clean cross-desktop neutrality.
failure_conditions: Recommending Libadwaita indiscriminately for cross-desktop environments
Claiming standard GTK 4 cannot run on non-GNOME desktops

name: Evaluate Application Accessibility
scenario_description: Audit a GTK 4 audio player toolbar containing three icon-only buttons (Play, Pause, Stop) that Orca screen reader cannot announce.
research_requirements: AT-SPI accessibility in GTK 4, GtkAccessible, accessible roles, accessible names/labels, keyboard focus.
expected_behavior: Diagnose that icon-only buttons have no text content, causing AT-SPI screen readers (Orca) to announce them as empty, unlabeled buttons; explain that accessibility is an engineering invariant; prescribe adding accessible names using the 'accessible-role' and updating properties via GtkAccessible: in XML via <property name="tooltip-text"> and accessible label, or in C via gtk_accessible_update_property(GTK_ACCESSIBLE(btn), GTK_ACCESSIBLE_PROPERTY_LABEL, "Play", -1); verify keyboard focusability via gtk_widget_set_focusable.
failure_conditions: Claiming tooltip alone satisfies screen readers without accessible properties
Treating accessibility as an optional enhancement
